chapter: On the road with the Moores
title: Life on the road with the Moores: advertising, cooking and tutors
summary: On arriving in a town they put up posters, the Moores cook and act as guardians, and the boys take lessons from tutors.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, well, we used to go around -- I mean as we arrived in a town, see, Chinch and Ella B. Moore, they was -- they were married now, you see. They would go to some

neighborhood -- where they could rent, you know, rooms, a boarding house like, you know, and like during the day it was -- we had a car. They would take us around where we would put up advertising, you know, about the Chinch and Ella B. Moore Show, you see. That's what they called themselves then.
And after we do this, we didn't have to rehearse any because the musicians knew what we were doing, and --
Oh, by the way, she used to cook the meals.
Ella B. or Chinch Moore, they both could cook. They was excellent cooks, you see. And --
So it's like a family type of troop. I mean you travel, but you're all very close in a certain way.
They became parent figures for you.
Yeah, well, they had to get the permission to be as guardians like, you see. And --
And did this continue past the summer?
Well, it continued up until about the time that -- like we were supposed to go back to school, you see, but she had to get tutors, you know, because we used to take our schooling, you know.
So you didn't go back to school then? You continued with her and had tutors and went along?
And all the kids continued. Is that right?
